definitions.explanation: A regular private residence, as opposed to public buildings, commercial properties, or government structures.
A traditional Japanese residential building, often with historical or architectural significance. These traditional farmhouses and townhouses are studied and preserved as cultural heritage.

examples.japanese: {火事|かじ}で{近|ちか}くの{民家|みんか}にも{被害|ひがい}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: The fire also caused damage to nearby private houses.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}のすぐ{下|した}に{民家|みんか}が{建|た}っている。
examples.english: There are private houses built right below the cliff.

examples.japanese: {熊|くま}が{民家|みんか}の{近|ちか}くに{出没|しゅつぼつ}したとの{報告|ほうこく}があった。
examples.english: There was a report of a bear appearing near residential houses.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{民家|みんか}をカフェに{改装|かいそう}した。
examples.english: They renovated an old folk house into a cafe.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}には{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}の{民家|みんか}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: There are folk houses from the Edo period remaining in this area.

examples.japanese: {民家|みんか}を{移築|いちく}して{保存|ほぞん}する{野外|やがい}{博物館|はくぶつかん}を{見学|けんがく}した。
examples.english: I visited an open-air museum that relocates and preserves traditional folk houses.

notes:
USAGE:
In news reports, {民家|みんか} is the standard word for "private house" when describing disasters, crime scenes, or wildlife sightings near residential areas. In architectural and cultural contexts, it refers specifically to traditional Japanese vernacular housing ({古|ふる}{民家|みんか}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {民家|みんか}に{被害|ひがい}: damage to private houses
- {古|ふる}{民家|みんか}: old folk house
- {民家|みんか}{再生|さいせい}: folk house renovation/revival
- {民家|みんか}を{改装|かいそう}する: to renovate a folk house

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {住宅|じゅうたく}: residence, housing (more general, includes apartments)
- {家屋|かおく}: building, house (formal, used in legal/insurance contexts)
- {一戸建|いっこだ}て: detached house (modern standalone house)
